reference_sql:
WITH months AS (
  -- one row per month of 2024
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start AS month
  FROM calendar
  WHERE cal_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31'
), channels AS (
  -- one row per order channel
  SELECT DISTINCT channel
  FROM orders
), monthly AS (
  -- one row per channel and month with orders
  SELECT channel, CAST(date_trunc('month', order_ts) AS DATE) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY channel, CAST(date_trunc('month', order_ts) AS DATE)
)
SELECT c.channel, m.month, COALESCE(o.orders, 0) AS orders
FROM channels c
CROSS JOIN months m
LEFT JOIN monthly o ON o.channel = c.channel AND o.month = m.month

other_way.tradeoff: A count subquery per cell of the grid needs no outer join, but it counts the orders again for every channel and month.

solver.query:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT CAST(d AS DATE) AS month FROM generate_series(DATE '2024-01-01', DATE '2024-12-01', INTERVAL 1 MONTH) t(d)
), chans AS (
  SELECT 'store' AS channel UNION ALL SELECT 'web'
), o AS (
  SELECT channel, CAST(date_trunc('month', order_ts) AS DATE) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT c.channel, m.month, COALESCE(o.orders, 0) AS orders
FROM chans c CROSS JOIN months m
LEFT JOIN o ON o.channel = c.channel AND o.month = m.month
